You said:
How to prepare for sales executive Interview by pd classes Manoj Sharma interview specialist 
ChatGPT said:
Preparing for a Sales Executive Interview under the guidance of PD Classes (Manoj Sharma) can be very strategic and effective. Here's a focused approach inspired by his teaching style and common interview expectations:

1. Self-Introduction (PD  classes Style)
Prepare a powerful self-introduction using PD Classes format:

Name, Qualification

Hometown & Family background

Key strengths & hobbies

Why sales?

Example:
“My name is Devansh Reddy. I have completed my graduation in [your stream]. I belong to Tirupati, known for its spiritual heritage. My strengths are communication, adaptability, and a positive attitude. I enjoy interacting with new people, which naturally draws me to a sales career…”

2. Knowledge of Sales Concepts
Understand and be ready to speak on:

What is sales?

Difference between sales and marketing

Steps of a sales process (AIDA model: Attention, Interest, Desire, Action)

What is B2B and B2C sales?

Product vs service selling
#salesexecutive 
3. Common Interview Questions
PD Classes often focus on expected Q&A practice, such as:

Why do you want to become a sales executive?

How will you convince a customer to buy your product?

How do you handle rejection?

Sell me this pen/bottle technique (demo your persuasion skills)
#salesmanager 
4. PD Classes Style Mock Interviews
Practice in front of a mirror or with a friend:

Use body language, smile, confidence

Speak with fluency and clarity

Keep answers short, specific, and positive

5. Learn from Real Interview Simulations (PD Videos)
Watch Manoj Sharma Sir’s YouTube videos:

Search: “Sales Executive Interview by PD Classes”

Observe candidate replies and Sir’s corrections

Note his tips on voice modulation, content structuring, and handling pressure
sales executive Interview Questions and answers by Manoj Sharma interview specialist pd classes 
6. Sales Vocabulary (Buzzwords)
Use some smart terms:

Lead generation

Conversion ratio

Customer retention

Target vs achievement

USP (Unique Selling Proposition)

7. Prepare for Company-Specific Questions
Research about the company:
